Brands whose share of voice exceeds their market share tend to grow over time, which makes share of voice a leading indicator rather than a vanity metric. Social listening tools like Lumen in Hootsuite Social OS can support share of voice tracking across channels and competitors. Measuring share of voice is only half the job. Growing it comes down to consistent posting, conversation-worthy content, fast responses, smart budget decisions, and employee advocacy. What is share of voice? Share of voice is a way of measuring your brand’s visibility compared to your competitors. It’s a great metric to focus on if you’re looking to increase brand awareness or sales. This pie chart shows how share of voice splits among four competitors. In the past, share of voice was used to measure the success of your paid advertising . Now the definition covers overall online visibility: social media mentions, news and blog coverage, where you show up in organic search, and how often your ads appear. It’s also more than a visibility score. Research from Les Binet and Peter Field, published by the IPA in The Long and the Short of It , popularised the idea of “excess share of voice,” which holds that when a brand’s share of voice is higher than its share of market, the brand tends to gain market share over time. The reverse is also true. That relationship is why marketing leaders treat share of voice as an early signal of where the business is heading, not just a snapshot of who is loudest. In other words, traditional share of voice tracks what brands say about themselves, and social share of voice tracks what people say about brands. I can build a (pretty good, if I do say so myself) carousel in Canva or even Figma. But I can't draw, and I can't create the kind of illustrations I see other creators using across their content. That turned out to be exactly the gap where AI image generators are most useful — not replacing photography, but creating visuals I couldn't make on my own. So I tested nine of them on three things I'd actually use for social media: an illustrated sticker sheet, a styled product shot, and a text-based graphic. If you just want the short answer, Nano Banana 2 was the most consistent across all three, and Seedream and Ideogram 3.0 were the most reliable with text. smm_pool.text: As Buffer has continued to support the individuals, creators, and small and medium businesses who use us, we've had to balance being a relatively small team with making tough decisions. We've had to make one of these recently. After careful deliberation as a team, we've decided to retire Start Page. If you've built a Start Page with us, thank you. Creators, small businesses, and nonprofits have used it as a front door to their work since 2021. Many of our customers were just getting started with their online journey, and a full website can be expensive and fiddly to maintain. Start Page provided a simple, flexible page anyone could build in minutes and share across their social profiles. We don't take ending that lightly, which is why we're giving several months' notice, firm dates, and multiple options to make the transition as hassle-free as possible Here's the timeline: November 4, 2026: We've stopped allowing the creation of new Start Pages November 30, 2026: You'll have tools to move your page somewhere else. February 2, 2027: We'll begin taking down Start Pages that haven't been migrated somewhere else. I'd like to elaborate on why we're doing this, the plan moving forward, and what options we plan to have available. Why we're doing this Having one link that holds everything (also referred to as a link-in-bio tool) is still useful in today's social space. So why are we moving away from it? For us at Buffer, three things have become hard to ignore. We've focused Buffer on our core strengths outside of Start Page. Buffer is a social media toolkit: we help you plan, publish, and learn from your content, and engage with your community across the social channels you use. While Start Page lives in your bio, it sits off to the side of all that. We've wanted to work on Start Page, but it takes away from Buffer's strengths and focus. From a capabilities perspective, Start Page has fallen behind, and catching up would cost us the things you rely on. Link-in-bio and microsite tools have come a long way since 2021, and Start Page hasn't kept pace. Making it best-in-class would mean pulling several teammates away from other key, much-requested improvements to other core Buffer features. We don't think that's the right trade for most of our customers. It's challenging to run well as a small, nimble team.
